about.title: About Costa Rica Tree Atlas
about.subtitle: A privately maintained project documenting the magnificent trees of Costa Rica

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: The Costa Rica Tree Atlas is dedicated to creating a comprehensive, accessible, and bilingual resource documenting the remarkable trees found throughout Costa Rica. We believe that knowledge about native flora is essential for conservation, education, and fostering a deeper appreciation for the natural world.

bilingual.title: Bilingual Content
bilingual.description: All content is available in both English and Spanish, making this resource accessible to a wider audience.

comprehensive.title: Comprehensive Profiles

openSource.title: Community Collaboration

whyCostaRica.title: Why Costa Rica?
whyCostaRica.description: Despite being only 0.03% of Earth's surface, Costa Rica contains nearly 5% of the world's biodiversity. This remarkable concentration of life makes it one of the most important places on Earth for conservation and biological research.

seasonal.title: Seasonal Calendar - Costa Rica Tree Atlas
seasonal.description: Discover when Costa Rica's trees flower and fruit throughout the year. Plan your nature visits with our phenological calendar.
seasonal.pageDescription: Discover when Costa Rica's trees are flowering and fruiting throughout the year. Includes local holidays and environmental events.
seasonal.climateDescription: Costa Rica has two main seasons that influence tree flowering and fruiting patterns. The dry season triggers many species to flower, while the wet season supports fruit development.
seasonal.drySeasonNote: Peak flowering season for many species. Many deciduous trees lose their leaves and produce spectacular blooms.
seasonal.wetSeasonNote: Primary fruiting season. Abundant rainfall supports fruit development and dispersal by animals.
seasonal.eventsDescription: Costa Rica's holidays and environmental events throughout the year, many connected to the country's rich tree heritage.

warnings.criticalMessage: This tree poses extreme danger. All parts are highly toxic and can cause serious injury or death. DO NOT touch, eat, or burn. Seek immediate medical attention if exposed.
warnings.severeMessage: This tree is highly dangerous. Toxic parts can cause severe poisoning, chemical burns, or serious injury. Avoid contact and keep children and pets away.
warnings.highMessage: This tree contains toxic substances that can cause poisoning or injury. Exercise caution and avoid ingestion of any plant parts.
warnings.moderateMessage: This tree may cause mild to moderate reactions. Use caution around children and pets.

firstAid.title: First Aid & Emergency Response
firstAid.ingestion: If ingested, seek immediate medical attention. Do not induce vomiting unless directed by medical professional.
firstAid.skinContact: If sap contacts skin, wash immediately with soap and water. Seek medical attention if blistering or severe irritation occurs.
firstAid.eyeContact: If sap enters eyes, flush immediately with clean water for 15 minutes and seek emergency medical care.

disclaimer.title: Safety Information Disclaimer
disclaimer.content: Safety information is provided for educational purposes only. Individual reactions may vary significantly based on age, health status, amount of exposure, and individual sensitivity. Always supervise children around plants. Consult a medical professional or certified arborist for specific concerns. The Costa Rica Tree Atlas is not liable for injuries or damages resulting from interaction with trees described in this guide.
disclaimer.sources: Information compiled from authoritative toxicology sources, scientific literature, and medical case reports.
disclaimer.emergency: Seek immediate medical attention if poisoning occurs
